covers: The XMS driver: every function the emulator's XMS_Handler has a case for. The driver is called far through the address INT 2Fh AX=4310h returns, with the function in AH, so the key is `0x43/<AH>` (43h is the multiplex number that finds the driver).

entries.name: get xms version
entries.description: Returns the XMS specification version, the driver revision and whether the HMA exists.
entries.behaviour: Returns AX=0300h (XMS 3.00), BX=0301h (the driver revision) and DX=1 if the HMA exists (the hma option) or 0 if not. BL is not touched.

entries.name: request hma
entries.description: Asks the driver for the high memory area.
entries.behaviour: DX = bytes wanted. Success: AX=1 and the HMA is marked as held by the caller; BL is not touched. Failure: AX=0 and BL=90h if there is no HMA, 91h if an application or the DOS kernel already holds it, 92h if DX is below the hma minimum allocation.

entries.name: release hma
entries.description: Gives the high memory area back to the driver.
entries.behaviour: AX=1 and the HMA is released if an application holds it. Otherwise AX=0 and BL=93h (not allocated), or BL=90h if there is no HMA. If the DOS kernel occupies the HMA the emulator logs a warning and answers the same way.

entries.name: global enable a20
entries.description: Turns the A20 gate on for the HMA and keeps it on until the global disable.
entries.behaviour: The first call raises the local enable count and switches A20 on if the count was 0; later calls do nothing. Returns AX=1 and BL=00h. No error is ever returned.

entries.name: global disable a20
entries.description: Undoes the global A20 enable.
entries.behaviour: If A20 was globally enabled it lowers the local enable count, switching A20 off at 0, and returns AX=1, BL=00h; if the count is already 0 it returns AX=0, BL=82h. If it was not globally enabled it returns AX=1, BL=00h.
entries.differs: The list gives 94h when the A20 line is still enabled; the emulator never returns 94h, only 82h.

entries.name: query a20
entries.description: Tells whether the A20 gate is enabled.
entries.behaviour: Returns AX=1 if A20 is enabled and AX=0 if not, with BL=00h. A20 is read from port 92h bit 1 (on PC-98, port F2h bit 0 clear means enabled).

entries.behaviour: DX = handle. Success: AX=1, BL=00h and the block is freed. Failure: AX=0 and BL=A2h if the handle is 0, out of range or not in use, or ABh if the block is locked.

entries.name: move ext memory
entries.description: Copies a block of memory between conventional and extended memory according to a move structure.
entries.behaviour: DS:SI = structure (length, source and destination handle and offset); handle 0 means a segment:offset address. Success: AX=1, BL untouched, A20 forced on during the copy. Failure: AX=0 and BL=A3h or A5h bad source or destination handle, A4h or A6h bad offset, A7h odd length, length past the block, or real end past 10FFF0h.
entries.differs: The list gives A8h for an invalid overlap and 80h to 82h; the emulator never returns them and copies overlapping ranges with no check.

entries.name: lock ext memory
entries.description: Locks an extended memory block and returns its physical address.
entries.behaviour: DX = handle. Success: AX=1 and DX:BX = the 32-bit physical address, with the lock count raised by one up to 255. Failure: AX=0 and BL=A2h for an invalid handle.
entries.differs: The list gives ACh when the lock count overflows; the emulator stops the count at 255 and returns success.

entries.name: request umb
entries.description: Allocates an upper memory block of DX paragraphs.
entries.behaviour: Works only with the umb option on, else AX=0 and BL=80h. Success: AX=1 and BX = segment. Failure: AX=0 and BL=B1h with DX=0 if none is free, or B0h with DX = the largest block if only a smaller one is.
entries.differs: The list returns the actual block size in DX on success; the emulator does not write DX.

entries.description: Frees an upper memory block given by its segment.
entries.behaviour: DX = segment. Works only with the umb option on, else AX=0 and BL=80h. If DOS frees the block AX=1; any failure gives AX=0 and BL=B1h.
entries.differs: The list gives B2h for an invalid UMB segment; the emulator returns B1h.

entries.description: Returns the largest free block, the total free memory and the highest memory address, with 32-bit sizes.
